1. Introduction 
 
A new Biodiversity Action Plan (BAP) is being prepared for County Westmeath in partnership with the 
Heritage Council, in accordance with national policy objectives to promote and protect Ireland’s 
natural heritage. The preparation of this Plan is also a statutory requirement under the Fourth 
National Biodiversity Action Plan (2023–2030), which requires all local authorities to develop and 
implement local biodiversity action plans by 2026. The BAP sets out Westmeath County Council’s 
commitment to protecting, conserving, and enhancing biodiversity across the County. It provides a 
clear framework for coordinated action and partnership, over the lifetime of the Plan. The aim of the 
BAP is to protect and enhance biodiversity, strengthen ecosystem resilience, respond to the 
challenges of climate change, thus safeguarding the natural environment for our future generations. 
 
The Plan builds on national and international biodiversity strategies and aligns with the National 
Biodiversity Action Plan, the EU Biodiversity Strategy, the Westmeath County Development Plan 
2021-2027 and other relevant policy frameworks. 
 
The purpose of this Chief Executive’s Report is to provide an overview of the public consultation 
undertaken at both the pre-draft and draft stages of the Westmeath Biodiversity Action Plan process, 
outline the content of the submissions received and set out the Council’s responses to the 
submissions and recommendations arising from same.  
 
 
2. Overview of the Stage 1 Consultation Process on the Issues Paper  
 
A Biodiversity Issues Paper which sets out the key biodiversity issues relating to Westmeath was prepared 
to stimulate interest and encourage public participation at this initial stage in the plan process.  Public 
Consultation on the Issues Paper took place from 5 March to 17 April 2024. The Biodiversity Office 
facilitated 4 number information sessions events in Mullingar, Athlone, Moate and Castlepollard 
libraries with a total of 24 people attending. Thirty written submissions were received via the 
Council’s online consultation portal, and 22 questionnaires were completed at library events.  
The Issues Paper was advertised in the local press, was placed on the Council’s social media 
platforms and circulated to both Public Participation Network (PPN) and a number of stakeholder 
consultees listed in Appendix 1.

Submissions were received from members of the public, community groups, and statutory bodies, 
and covered a broad range of biodiversity-related themes. Key issues raised are highlighted in Figure 
1 above. Many submissions specified the need for enhanced habitats and species mapping, 
woodland conservation and regeneration, the use of evidence-based approaches to biodiversity 
management, and the importance of adopting a whole-of-society approach to nature protection. 
Respondents also emphasised the importance of education, training, and awareness initiatives, and 
called for targeted species surveys to inform local action. The above issues and insights were 
carefully considered and have informed the vision, objectives and actions of the Draft Plan. 
 
A presentation was given to the Planning and Transport Strategic Policy Committee on 21 March 
2024, outlining the content of the Biodiversity Issues Paper together with information in engaging 
with the Pre-Draft BAP process.   
 
3. Overview of the Stage 2 Draft Westmeath BAP 2025-2031 Public 
Consultation 
Following completion of the Issues Paper consultation and consideration of the submissions 
received, the Draft Westmeath Biodiversity Action Plan 2025–2031 was prepared in collaboration 
with the Heritage Council and the Westmeath Biodiversity Working Group. The Draft Plan builds on 
the priorities identified during Stage 1 process and sets out a framework of objectives and actions to 
protect, conserve, and enhance biodiversity across the County. It reflects local and national policy 
commitments and incorporates measures that promote community engagement, education, and 
the conservation and regeneration of natural habitats based on evidence-led biodiversity 
management. 
The Draft Biodiversity Action Plan 2025–2031 was placed on public consultation from 3 June to 1 July 
2025. Both the Draft Plan and associated Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) and 
Appropriate Assessment (AA) Screening Reports were circulated to the list of prescribed stakeholder 
consultees in Appendix 1, were made available on the Council’s website, and were displayed in all 
branch libraries. The consultation was also promoted through the Public Participation Network 
(PPN), representing over 900 community and voluntary groups across the county, to ensure broad 
community awareness and engagement. Submissions were invited from individuals, community 
groups, and organisations. 
Public information sessions on the Draft BAP were also held at Mullingar, Moate, Athlone and 
Castlepollard libraries. These in-person public consultation sessions were very well attended.  
Participants expressed strong support for the Draft Plan and a clear willingness to be actively 
involved in biodiversity actions and events across Westmeath. 
The consultation was promoted via local newspaper notices and weekly social-media posts on 
Instagram and X. With over 5,100 views across both platforms, the consultation content reached a 
significant audience. Combined, the two platforms achieved a total of 5,107 views, 3,495 reach, and 
46 interactions.  
Fifteen written submissions were received. Issues raised included the need to strengthen habitat 
protection and restoration measures, enhance biodiversity data and mapping, and promote 
community-led biodiversity projects. Other themes highlighted the importance of education and 
awareness, continued inter-agency collaboration, and the need to support the integration of 
biodiversity considerations into land-use and development planning through guidance, training, and 
information-sharing. 
Throughout both consultation stages, the Westmeath Biodiversity Working Group met regularly to 
guide the process, review submissions, and consolidate input from statutory and public

stakeholders. Feedback from this stage directly informed the preparation of the Westmeath 
Biodiversity Action Plan 2025–2031. 
A briefing was also provided to the Planning and Transport SPC on 22 May 2025, outlining the 
contents of the Draft Plan and the consultation process. 
The Issues raised in the 15 submissions were categorised in accordance with the chapters of the 
Draft BAP under the headings of Biodiversity, Challenges and Opportunities, Objectives and Actions, 
and Delivering the Plan. The feedback provided valuable insights into community and stakeholder 
perspectives on the key issues, opportunities, and delivery mechanisms for biodiversity action 
within the county and informed the refinement of the Draft Westmeath Biodiversity Action Plan 
2025–2031. Figure 2 below provides an overview of the number of submissions received under each 
theme. 
 
 
 
 
Figure 2. Submissions received on the Draft BAP 
 
Submissions from both stakeholders and community members expressed strong support for the 
Draft Biodiversity Action Plan, highlighting priorities around species, habitats, designated sites, and 
county and local biodiversity areas. Many emphasised the importance of effective delivery, including 
clearer communication of biodiversity’s value, increased community involvement, and greater 
support for citizen science. Key pressures such as land-use change, invasive species, and climate 
change were identified, alongside opportunities for awareness, heritage, creativity, and habitat 
restoration. Submissions also called for balancing development with biodiversity protection and 
enhancing urban greening to support climate resilience and community wellbeing. Overall, the 
submissions provided valuable feedback that refined the Plan and guide its delivery across the 
county.

Minor amendments are proposed to the Draft Westmeath Biodiversity Action Plan to ensure 
consistency, clarity, and alignment with current policy and guidance. These updates include minor 
textual and contextual edits, updated references, and the inclusion of supporting information where 
appropriate. The amendments do not alter the intent, actions, or objectives of the Plan and are 
considered non-material in nature. 
 
 
4.  
Chief Executive’s Response and Recommendations 
 
Following the review of submissions received, one amendment is proposed to the Draft Westmeath 
Biodiversity Action Plan 2025–2031: 
Amend Action 4.10 Expand the scope of this action to implement the forthcoming Tree Management 
policy and Hedgerow Management Policy to support best practice management and training within 
relevant Council departments, including Roads and Environment. The single amendment (Action 
4.10) strengthens the integration of biodiversity management across Council operations, 
particularly regarding hedgerow and tree maintenance.

All other issues raised are either incorporated within the Plan or relate to matters outside the remit 
of the Biodiversity Action Plan.  
 
The actions of the Draft Westmeath Biodiversity Action Plan have been screened for the need to 
undertake both Strategic Environmental Assessment (SEA) and Appropriate Assessment (AA). It has 
been determined that no significant environmental effects have been identified from the 
implementation of the actions and that no further assessment is required. 
 
 
5. Recommendation for Approval  
 
The Biodiversity Action Plan has been prepared in conjunction with the Biodiversity Working Group. 
The public consultation process for the Draft Westmeath Biodiversity Action Plan 2025–2031 
demonstrated strong local interest and engagement from individuals, communities, and statutory 
agencies in the plan making process. The submissions received have provided valuable insights into 
local biodiversity issues and have informed the content of the plan.  
 
The Westmeath Biodiversity Action Plan 2025-2031 sets out a structured approach for conserving 
and enhancing biodiversity in Westmeath, including the Council’s commitment, in collaboration 
with key stakeholders, to implement clearly defined actions over the six-year duration of the plan. I 
seek your endorsement of the Westmeath Biodiversity Action Plan 2025-2031 as presented, subject 
to amendment recommended above.

Barry Kehoe
